title: Battery management system DFMEA
goal: Present safety-relevant BMS failure modes, controls, and computed risk priorities.

rubric.must: The worksheet visibly identifies the battery management system and its safe-limit monitoring function.
Overcharge protection failure visibly links to thermal runaway or pack fire with severity 10.
Each visible failure row has severity, occurrence, detection, and computed RPN or action-priority fields.
The safety-critical overcharge rows are visibly highlighted as high priority.
Delayed overtemperature detection and incorrect state-of-charge estimation are visibly included as separate modes.
Redundant sensing, software assurance, diagnostics, or validation controls are visibly listed.
The worksheet uses readable aligned columns and distinguishes risk cells visually.

ideal.notes: Independently authored against visual-eval/exemplars/fmea/ideal.svg (sha256 656f156ad4fb), source sha256 6ee8a3b46885. Independent worksheet with all causes, effects, controls and scores. Adjacent repeated cells merged; AP or RPN follows the source ranking method. AP values checked against the AIAG-VDA 2019 matrix documented by HBK ReliaSoft, https://reliasoftcloud.hbkworld.com/demo/help/content/risk_ranking_logic.htm, not the engine approximation. RPN is multiplied independently; no AP invented for the RPN-only case. All 21 risk-batch targets were rasterised with Resvg and visually inspected individually on 2026-09-14; this drawing was accepted for geometry, label readability and semantic traceability. Provisional because existing rubric high-priority-safety incorrectly requires High AP for S10/O2/D3 and S10/O2/D4; verified matrix gives Low, while thermal calibration S8/O4/D5 gives Medium. Target preserves correct source-derived values; rubric needs correction.
